Michael Pollan that explores the co-evolutionary, reciprocal relationship between humans and domesticated plants. It proposes that plants use human desires—specifically sweetness, beauty, intoxication, and control—to manipulate us into spreading their genes globally.

The Poisonwood Bible is a story told by the wife and four daughters of Nathan Price, a fierce, evangelical Baptist who takes his family and mission to the Belgian Congo in 1959. They carry with them everything they believe they will need from home, but soon find that all of it - from garden seeds to Scripture - is calamitously transformed on African soil. What follows is a suspenseful epic of one family's tragic undoing and remarkable reconstruction over the course of three decades in postcolonial Africa.
